title: Acne
summary: A common skin condition that causes pimples, blackheads and whiteheads.

sections.heading: What is Acne?
sections.body: A common skin condition that causes pimples, blackheads and whiteheads.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.body: Clogged pores due to oil, dead skin cells and bacteria.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.body: Over-the-counter products, prescription creams or oral medications.

sections.heading: Management
sections.body: Gentle skincare routine and avoiding picking at the skin.

faq.a: Acne is caused by clogged pores, bacteria, excess oil production, hormonal imbalances, and sometimes lifestyle or dietary factors.

title: Allergy
summary: An overreaction of the immune system to substances like pollen, dust or certain foods.

sections.heading: What is it?
sections.body: An overreaction of the immune system to substances like pollen, dust or certain foods.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Itching, redness, swelling, hives or rash.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.body: Avoid triggers, use antihistamines and apply topical creams.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor
sections.body: If symptoms persist or are severe.

title: Hyperhidrosis
summary: Excessive sweating beyond normal levels.

sections.heading: What is Hyperhidrosis?
sections.body: Excessive sweating beyond normal levels.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Persistent sweating, especially on the palms, feet, underarms or face.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.body: Antiperspirants, Botox injections or prescription medications.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor
sections.body: If sweating affects daily life or causes distress.

title: Pigmentation
summary: Dark or light spots on the skin due to excess or lack of melanin.

sections.heading: What is Pigmentation?
sections.body: Dark or light spots on the skin due to excess or lack of melanin.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.body: Sun exposure, aging, hormonal changes or inflammation.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.body: Topical creams, chemical peels or laser therapy to lighten spots.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.body: Regular use of sunscreen and avoiding direct sun exposure.

title: Psoriasis
summary: A chronic skin condition causing red, scaly patches.

sections.heading: What is Psoriasis?
sections.body: A chronic skin condition causing red, scaly patches.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Thick, silvery scales on the skin, often on the elbows, knees and scalp.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.body: Topical creams, light therapy and medications to reduce inflammation.

sections.heading: Management
sections.body: Regular moisturizing and avoiding triggers like stress.

title: Urticaria
summary: Also known as hives, it's a skin reaction causing itchy wheals.

sections.heading: What is Urticaria?
sections.body: Also known as hives, it's a skin reaction causing itchy wheals.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Red, raised and itchy welts on the skin that can vary in size.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.body: Antihistamines, avoiding triggers and using soothing creams.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor
sections.body: If hives last more than a few days or cause difficulty breathing.

title: Vitiligo
summary: A condition where the skin loses its pigment, leading to white patches.

sections.heading: What is Vitiligo?
sections.body: A condition where the skin loses its pigment, leading to white patches.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: White patches of skin, often on the face, hands and other exposed areas.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.body: Topical creams, light therapy and sometimes skin camouflage or depigmentation therapy.

sections.body: Sun protection and regular skin monitoring.

summary: A laser treatment used primarily for skin conditions like psoriasis and vitiligo.

sections.heading: What is Laser Excimer?
sections.body: A laser treatment used primarily for skin conditions like psoriasis and vitiligo.

title: Excessive Hair Loss
summary: Noticeable hair thinning or bald spots.

sections.heading: What is Excessive Hair Loss?
sections.body: Noticeable hair thinning or bald spots.

sections.heading: Common Causes
sections.body: Stress, hormonal changes, genetics, poor nutrition or underlying health issues.

sections.heading: Self-Care Tips
sections.body: Maintain a healthy diet, reduce stress and avoid harsh hair treatments.

sections.heading: Over-the-counter Options
sections.body: Consider Minoxidil (Rogaine) for promoting hair regrowth.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor

title: GFC/PRP for Hair Growth
summary: Growth Factor Concentrate (GFC) or Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) therapy involves using your blood’s growth factors to stimulate hair growth.

sections.heading: What is GFC/PRP?
sections.body: Growth Factor Concentrate (GFC) or Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) therapy involves using your blood’s growth factors to stimulate hair growth.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A small amount of your blood is processed to concentrate growth factors, then injected into the scalp.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.body: Can improve hair density, reduce hair loss and promote natural hair growth.

sections.heading: Treatment duration
sections.body: Usually requires multiple sessions for optimal results.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Minimally invasive with low risk of side effects.

title: Hair Transplant
summary: A surgical procedure where hair follicles are removed from a donor area (usually the back of the head) to thinning or bald areas.

sections.heading: What is Hair Transplant?
sections.body: A surgical procedure where hair follicles are removed from a donor area (usually the back of the head) to thinning or bald areas.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Hair follicles are carefully transplanted to mimic natural hair growth.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.body: Provides a permanent solution to hair loss with natural-looking results.

sections.heading: Recovery
sections.body: Some downtime required with full results visible within 6-12 months.

sections.heading: Who it is for
sections.body: Ideal for those with significant hair loss who are suitable candidates for surgery.

faq.q: How long does a Hair Transplant last?
faq.a: The results of a hair transplant are permanent because the transplanted hair follows the natural growth cycle and does not fall out again.
The procedure is performed under local anesthesia, so it is almost pain-free. Patients may feel mild discomfort only during the healing phase.

faq.q: How long is the recovery time after a Hair Transplant?
faq.a: Usually, the scalp heals within 7–10 days, and patients can return to their normal routine quickly.

faq.q: Do I need additional treatments after a Hair Transplant?
faq.a: Some patients choose advanced treatments like Laser Therapy or PRP to improve scalp health and achieve faster, better results.

faq.q: When will new hair start growing after a Hair Transplant?
faq.a: Some patients choose advanced treatments like Laser Therapy or PRP to improve scalp health and achieve faster, better results.
